notes: Steven Piano now keeps itself up to date: a new version shows on the Piano tab, and on the school tablet it installs without a tap. Share diagnostics sends the app's logs when something goes wrong.

Channels play your library without end: Calm, Epic, Baroque, Romantic, Impressionist, Nocturnes, Études and Everything, each at its own volume. Popular, Recognisable and Epic on piano fill themselves from your pieces. Left alone for a minute, the tablet becomes a display for passers-by. Every piece starts after a short pause, the score lights the notes it plays in yellow, a mini player (a now-playing panel on tablets) keeps the piece in sight, the controls float on frosted glass, the Piano tab's settings are grouped into pages, and Appearance can follow the system or stay light or dark.

Web control: open the panel in any browser on your Tailscale network to see what is playing, play and queue pieces, browse the library, start channels, adjust the piano, and add pieces by dropping MIDI or zip files onto the page. Guests can request a piece by scanning the printable poster, one request every five minutes, with an approve-first switch. Turn it on under Piano › Remote control and set a six-digit PIN. Also: hardening from the security audit of the panel, a larger title on the standby screen, and small fixes.

Firmware updates from the app: Piano › Firmware and status shows the piano's firmware version, checks for a signed release, and sends it over Bluetooth — the piano goes quiet, receives the image, verifies the signature, restarts, and rolls back by itself if the new firmware fails to start. Needs firmware 2.0.0 on the piano first (one USB flash).

Kiosk mode for the school tablet: with the app as device owner, Piano › Kiosk makes the app the home screen and switches off Home, Recents, the shade and the lock screen; the tablet comes straight back into the app after a reboot. Hold the byline for three seconds and enter the PIN to unlock for a while or turn kiosk off. In kiosk, settings, disconnecting, imports and deletions ask for the PIN; playing, queueing and browsing stay free. Left alone, the tablet rests in display mode.

Schedules: Piano › Schedule plays a channel, a playlist or a piece on chosen days at a set time, until an end time or the end, at its own volume. The tablet wakes for it even with the screen off, connects to the piano and starts; a missed start is shown on the page. The web panel edits the same schedules, and a channel's long-press can schedule it. Also: firmware-update progress stays visible in kiosk, and button labels are consistent.

Studio: the tablet can transcribe a piano recording into a playable piece and compose new piano pieces by itself, both running on the tablet with no cloud service. Piano › Studio downloads the two models once (125 MB and 173 MB). Transcribe a recording… takes any audio the tablet plays; Compose a piece… takes a mood, key, tempo, length and a piece from your library to write in the manner of. Each result asks Keep or Discard after your first listen. Also: the app keeps its other device architectures, the security audit's hardening, and a denser composing budget.

The resting screen now shows the album art with the piece's title, composer and a few lines about it, and fades in and out slowly; Piano › Display › Standby shows lets you keep the paper roll instead.

Piano sound on the tablet: real recordings of an upright piano play what the app plays, with a volume control on Now playing and under Piano › Playback › Tablet sound — by default only while the piano isn't connected, or always if you choose. The sound file (57 MB, CC0) downloads once. The resting screen credits Wikipedia under a piece's notes.

Liquid Glass across the app: the headers, the tab bar and rail, the mini player, the transport, sheets, menus and dialogs are frosted surfaces the content scrolls under, with a soft fade where content meets a bar; the play control is a solid circle again; on the tablet the transport yields its blur while the library scrolls. Reduce transparency or high contrast text gives solid surfaces.

Steven Piano Cloud: the web panel from anywhere over HTTPS, without Tailscale. Piano › Remote control › CLOUD enrols the tablet with a code from the console, and the panel then lives at https://<relay>/p/<piano>/ behind the same PIN as before; the console (on Steven's own Cloudflare account, behind Cloudflare Access) lists every piano with its live dot and what it plays, and offers play, pause, next, stop, channels, the guest switches, Load the library, Rotate secret, Revoke and Forget, with an audit log. Steven's library: Load Steven's library on the empty Library and in the + sheet downloads 1,726 pieces (60 MB) from GitHub, checked against its hash, after a note on the licences; Update the library later adds only pieces never offered before. On the tablet, glass menus now stay inside their pane.
